thread:
support: :rotating_light: Customer RW-Cloud reported a spike of 502s + timeouts hitting hosted inference API around 11:10 UTC. ~18% p50->p99 jump for 30m. sending sample req_ids: rq_8f9a2, rq_8f9a9, rq_8fa12. Customer says errors started after a key rotation window.

alyssa: looking. can you drop the customer request ids and a sample full request/headers (redact sensitive)?

support: pasted one sanitized payload below, headers show Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>, x-customer-id: rw-xyz. also attaching the support ticket link: https://support.redwood.com/t/12345

support: ```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "rw-instruct-1b",
  "input": "summarize..."
}
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, x-request-id: rq_8f9a2
Response snippet: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream error: auth failed during handshake: token validation timeout"}
```

sam: initial metric check — spike aligns with 11:08-11:40 UTC. egress error rate on gateway p99 increased, auth service 504s around same time. looks like token validation path slowed.

alyssa: can someone run a traces query for rq_8f9a2 and one of the failing auth service spans? I'm seeing gaps in trace sampling for those minutes.

jordan: ran a short trace query, here's the span breakdown: gateway -> auth-proxy -> id-service -> kms. id-service spans show many long waits (8-12s). Traces for successful reqs show id-service ~40-120ms.

mat: @jordan can you paste the id-service logs around 11:10? suspect KMS client backoffs after rotation.

jordan: logs (sanitized):
```
2026-02-11T11:09:58Z id-service INFO validating token rq_8f9a2
2026-02-11T11:10:01Z id-service WARN kms call timeout (attempt 1) 
2026-02-11T11:10:03Z id-service WARN kms call timeout (attempt 2)
2026-02-11T11:10:07Z id-service ERROR KMS handshake failed, returning 502 proxied
2026-02-11T11:10:15Z id-service INFO retry succeeded
```

alyssa: that matches the timeline. ops-bot: did any infra deployments or KMS certificate rotations occur ~11:00?

ops-bot: Deployment activity: none. KMS automated rotation job started at 10:59:42 UTC (auto-rotate), rotation completed 11:12:08 UTC. Several clients logged transient timeouts while new keys propagated.

sam: hypothesis: KMS rotation created brief increase in latency for id-service KMS calls, causing auth-proxy to exceed its internal handshake timeout and bubble 502s back to gateway. Because token validation is in the critical path, that induced p99 client-facing timeouts.

support: customer impacted by 502s and some request retries. They asked if we can whitelist or fallback while rotation happens.

mat: mitigations we did/should do:
- short-term: increase id-service KMS call timeout and bounded retry window to avoid cascading into auth-proxy timeout (hotfix).
- mid-term: make auth-proxy fallback to previous key if KMS handshake fails during rotation for <=30s.
- alerting: create a dedicated SLO alert when id-service KMS call latency >1s sustained 5m.

alyssa: I can push the hotfix to id-service config (extend timeout from 2s->8s and reduce aggressive retry backoff) and roll to canary. Rolling now to canary-2.

jordan: can you also add a short-lived circuit breaker in auth-proxy to convert long KMS waits into 504 instead of 502? 502 is confusing for customers.

mat: agreed. 504 will show nicer semantics. I'll open a brief PR and link here. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/id-service/pull/452

sam: any signs of billing/authz mismatch? customer mentioned key rotation tied to billing KMS workflow. I don't see billing errors in logs — looks purely token validation latency.

support: customer notified. they want a postmortem and ETA for permanent fix for key-rotation resilience.

alyssa: putting together a short incident timeline and will include root cause (KMS rotation propagation + insufficient handshake fallback) and action items. Drafting now.

mat: follow-ups: add e2e test for KMS rotation case, update runbook for support to surface "KMS rotation window" to customers proactively.

jordan: metrics/query used for detection for runbook:
```
# logsql (our internal folded syntax)
select count(*) by status_code from gateway.logs where service="ingress" and timestamp between 2026-02-11T11:00 and 2026-02-11T11:30 group by status_code
# traces: trace.search("rq_8f9a2") -> show spans where id-service.duration > 1s
```
alyssa: final note: we need a short-lived alert tweak to suppress noisy SLO burn for 5xx that are KMS-rotation-caused (labelled rotation=true) so we don't trigger full-page for ~10m. I'll coordinate with oncall.

sam: thanks team. marking this as triaged. assigned to alyssa for postmortem + mat/jordan for fixes. :thumbsup:

support: customer updated: we applied a temporary mitigation and will follow up with timeline. closing support ticket once postmortem ready.
